title: A switch-on leads no mode when the arbiter's stale record matches the step's mode
claim: When the mode select changes while the supply reads off (the pump's own reset, a person) and the arbiter's record still holds the step's mode, the switch-on of a partial step lands with the hot-water mode in force; Heating follows one tick later.
mechanism: `_lead_mode` (#3420) calls `_write`, which returns early when `held.written['mode']` equals the target; `hold()`, which drops a record the entity no longer reads, never runs while the switch reads off (`_arbitrate` returns at `_pump_off`), so the record is stale exactly when the lead is needed.

evidence.unit: switch-on with the wrong mode in force (cell3530_record_wrong_mode_at_on)
evidence.machine: box B11 (shared container, Linux 6.18, ~/venv-ci Python 3.14.7, hastub)

perturbation.change: hold(coord, now) before the _write in _lead_mode (--perturb lead-hold)

metric_definition: mode select state in force at the supply switch-on of a heating step, against the step's mode from the plan (Heating where only space is booked)
phenomenon_property: A write skipped because the arbiter's record already holds it is skipped only when the entity reads that value.

null_control.note: same scenario with no change while off: the mode in force at switch-on is Heating (null arm 0)

reproduction_steps: partial (mode Heating recorded), idle (switch off), the select moved to DHW (Hot Water) at minute 35, partial at 45: switch_on at 45 with DHW in force, Heating written at 46
proposed_fix_scope: pump_arbiter._lead_mode: compare against the entity's reading (or run hold) before trusting the record.
